correctness.rationale: Under x=cos θ the measure is (2/π)sin²θ dθ and the second-kind basis is orthonormal by sine orthogonality. The real BV derivative measure represents the input modulo constants as a signed integral of unit jumps; Minkowski for the residual and equality at a maximizing jump reduce the norm to one scalar jump. The compact jump parameter has continuous residual, with zero at the endpoints and positive residual in the interior since a jump is not a polynomial almost everywhere. Direct integration gives p(θ) and the signed coefficients [sin(kθ)/k−sin((k+2)θ)/(k+2)]/π (the signed representative is used when differentiating their squares), with the stated full tail by Parseval. At π/2 reflection gives stationarity; differentiating the finite residual yields curvature coefficient 8[−1−floor(n/2)+Σ_{k odd≤n}(1+1/(k(k+2)))]. The sum of reciprocal products telescopes by 1/(k(k+2))=(1/k−1/(k+2))/2, verifying both exact signs and the degree-zero case. With N=n+2, square the leading tail coefficient −2 sinθ cos(mθ)/(πm); summability of the cross-error terms yields O(|cosθ|n^−2+n^−3) uniformly. The plain sum from N of m^−2 is n^−1−3/(2n²)+O(n^−3). Twice differencing the weights in the complex oscillatory sum gives its boundary term exp(2iNθ)/(N²(1−exp(2iθ))) with a uniform O(N^−3) error on compact interior arcs. On the endpoint arcs sin²θ≤1/4, the crude bound by the plain sum already keeps the leading residual below the centered residual. Uniform comparison on the remaining arc forces every maximizing angle to the midpoint. There the oscillatory term is at most (1+o(1))/(2n²) and the error from cosθ is o(n^−2). The even midpoint and odd angle π/2+π/(2N) align the leading phase and attain that upper expansion. At the midpoint without phase adjustment the boundary term carries (−1)^n, giving the exact parity-dependent second-order deficit. This proves the asymptotic norm, not a finite-cutoff optimizer classification.
correctness.replay: Independently compare the odd reciprocal-product sum to its telescoped expression using exact rational arithmetic for n=0–100. Evaluate the finite residual formula using 70-digit trigonometric arithmetic at the midpoint and at the phase-aligned witness for moderate and large cutoffs of each parity. For n=0 the maximum is R₀(π/2)=1/4; at n=1 the off-center extrema are near 1.1161343198 and 2.0254583338, with residual about 0.08221599166 versus 0.06987345130 at the midpoint. These diagnostics do not certify the asymptotic upper bound or exhaust extrema at general degree. The frozen checker.py was inspected, not executed.

value.rationale: The norm is a natural worst-case L² approximation benchmark for variation-bounded data under a canonical weight. The exact second term resolves a measurable failure of the midpoint choice at every odd degree, despite all optimal jump positions approaching the midpoint. This identifies a parity effect not seen in the leading error rate, with an explicit phase-aligned witness; it does not claim global finite-degree uniqueness.
